column2: The Tzar's secret police. The Chekist keeps lists of names and cellars beneath its houses, and it hunts the cultists, mutants and traitors who would open Kislev's gates to the north. Its agents wear plain grey coats and carry no seal, but every boyar knows them on sight. Kislev's gods have no Order of Sigmar. They have the Chekist.
The Master of the Chekist answers only to the Ice Throne, and some say not always to it.
Close to the Ice Throne in Kislev

The Court Chekist runs the crown's informers. He reads letters that are not his, listens at doors, and brings in the ones the crown wants taken. A ruler with a Chekist at court finds plots sooner. A ruler who lets the Chekist grow too strong may find himself on the Chekist's list.
This character serves the Chekist, the secret police of the Ice Throne, and hunts the enemies of Kislev who hide among its people.

This Tzarina bore Fearfrost against the hordes of Chaos and threw them back, as Khan-Queen Miska did when she led the Gospodars over the mountains. The boyars kneel lower before her, and the girls of her house are born with the frost in their blood more often.
A thick book bound in black leather, full of names in a small tight hand. Some of the names are crossed out. Every boyar who sees it on the table goes quiet.
A splinter of the ice from which the Ice Palace was raised again. It never melts, not even in the hand, and it hums faintly with the old magic of the Ice Queens.
The Court Chekist's informers listen in every tavern and corridor.
The Chekist has built a web of informers that answers to him. It hears everything. It may not tell the crown everything.
The Chekist made an arrest on the crown's order not long ago.
The Chekist asked for a house of its own not long ago.
The Ice Witches keep the Ice Palace whole with their magic, and the crown pays them for it every year in gold and favours.
The Court at the Bokha Palace
The court has moved to the Palace Gospodarin. It is warm, and the stewards love it, but the boyars whisper that the Ice Throne stands empty.
The Ice Palace is gone, and with it the old ways. This ruler rules by their own right, not by the Ice Witches' leave.
The Tzar spent a night in Ursun's cave and walked out at dawn. The priests say the Father of Bears has marked him.
The Tzar did not win against the enemies of Kislev in the years of his trial. The boyars say Ursun has turned away from him.
The Tzarina has refused a great boyar's suit, and the court talks of nothing else.
The crown called the Great Pulk not long ago.
This ruler seized or killed a guest who had eaten their bread and salt. In Kislev there is no lower thing a host can do.
The crown gave the Ice Queen's Ball not long ago.
The water of the melted Ice Palace has run down into the lower city. Cellars are full, the markets are mud, and the poor are angry.
A Guest at the Ice Queen's Ball

The hordes of Chaos are in the Tzardom. Call every boyar of Kislev to send his rota to the Great Pulk. Those who answer win the crown's favour. Those who refuse will be remembered. The pulk goes home when the war ends.
The Ice Palace is gone, but you are an Ice Witch and you sit the Ice Throne. Call the frost and raise it again, wall by wall, as the Ice Queens of old did.
Send the Court Chekist for this one. Cultists, mutants and those under suspicion are fair game. So is a vassal who speaks against the crown, though the other boyars will take note.

The Chekist came in the grey hour before dawn, as it always does. [chekist_quarry.GetTitledName] was taken from bed, still in a nightshirt, and is now in the cellars. The Court Chekist lays the papers on your table. The marks of the Ruinous Powers are all through them.

The Chekist came in the grey hour before dawn, as it always does. [chekist_quarry.GetTitledName] was taken from bed and is now in the cellars. There was no cult and no mutation. Only words spoken against the crown, and the Chekist heard them. The other boyars have heard about it by noon.

[chekist_officer.GetTitledName] stands before you with ink on his fingers and something darker under his nails. He took [chekist_victim.GetTitledName] to the cellars on the word of an informer. Three days on the rack and the boyar confessed to everything. Then the informer was found to owe the boyar money. The boyar is innocent, and the family knows it.
Say nothing. The Chekist does not make mistakes.

Your informers have an odd report. Some of the Chekist's men have been taking money and orders from [chekist_officer.GetTitledName] alone, and their reports never reach your table. The Chekist has built a web of his own. It is a very good web.
Let him. A good web is a good web.

A guard you have never seen before is at your door. Another is at the end of the corridor. A letter on your desk, unsigned, says that the boyars have long wondered whether the crown is fit to rule, and that [chekist_officer.GetTitledName] has the names of everyone who agrees. It does not ask for anything yet.

[chekist_officer.GetTitledName] asks for a castle. The Order of Sigmar has chapter houses in every city of the Empire, he says, and the Chekist has a back room. It needs a house of its own, with deep cellars, to hold those it takes. He has his eye on [chekist_house.GetName].

[Root.GetFirstName] walks alone through the halls of the Ice Palace, between walls that glow blue in the torchlight. At the end of the great hall the High Priestess of Ursun and the eldest of the Ice Witches set the frost crown on her head. It is so cold it burns. The boyars kneel, and their breath steams in the air. Kislev has a Tzarina again.

The Ice Palace is gone, so [Root.GetFirstName] is crowned in the great hall of the Palace Gospodarin. The frost crown is brought from its vault, and the old boyars mutter that it has never been set on a head in a warm room before. Still they kneel. Kislev has a Tzarina again.
For Kislev and the Ice Throne.

The Tzars of Kislev are crowned at the temple of Ursun, but first they spend a night alone in the god's cave in the hill beneath it. There is always a bear in that cave. The priests say Ursun chooses whether the Tzar walks out at dawn, and some Tzars have not. The boyars wait at the cave mouth with torches. [Root.GetFirstName] could be crowned without it. It has been done before. It has not been forgotten.
I need no bear to tell me I am Tzar.

The enemy broke and ran, and the priests of Ursun say it was the god's own roar that broke them. Ursun's Trial is passed. The boyars who said the new Tzar was too soft for the throne have gone very quiet.

Five years since the crowning, and the Tzar has won no battle against the enemies of Kislev. The priests of Ursun say nothing, which is worse than if they spoke. In the boyars' halls they say the god has turned away. One of them has already begun to talk of his own descent from the old Tzars.
Let them talk. I am still Tzar.

Water drips from the ceiling of the throne room. The Ice Palace stands because the magic of an Ice Witch holds it, and [Root.GetFirstName] is no Ice Witch. Already the carvings in the great hall are soft at the edges. The Sisterhood will keep it whole, for a price, every year. Or the court could move to the warm stone halls of the Bokha Palace and let the ice go slowly. Or it could be let go now, and with it the Ice Witches' hold on the crown.
Beg the Sisterhood to hold it.
Move the court to the Bokha Palace.
Let it melt. A new age begins.

It went all at once. A wall of the Ice Palace slid down the hill in the night, and the meltwater went with it into the lower city. Cellars are full, streets are rivers of mud, and the poor of Kislev are standing on their roofs. They are asking where the crown is.
The city will dig itself out.
No one has lived in the Ice Palace for years, and no Ice Witch has come to hold it. This spring the last of its towers fell in. The Ice Palace is gone.

[Root.GetFirstName] stands on the bare hill where the Ice Palace was, in the dead of winter, and calls the frost. It comes. The air turns to needles and the ground groans. By dawn there are walls, by the next night towers, and on the third day the Ice Palace stands again, blue and white and humming with cold. The people of Kislev come up the hill in their thousands to see it.

[tsar_suitor.GetTitledName] has come to court with fifty riders and a chest of furs and asked, before all the boyars, for the hand of the Tzarina. It is a great match. It is also a great house, and one that would sit very close to the Ice Throne. If he is refused before the whole court he will not forget it.
I accept. He comes to my court.
I refuse. The Tzarina rules alone.
I am wed to Kislev and to the ice.

The Chekist's men have watched [tsar_consort.GetFirstName] for months. The Tzarina's husband has been dining with boyars who would rather see a man on the Ice Throne, and he does not argue with them. Nothing has been done. Not yet.
Send him to the frontier to cool off.
Give him a seat at court and keep him close.

The hordes of the north came to Kislev, and [Root.GetFirstName] met them with Fearfrost in her hand and threw them back. The priests of Ursun and Dazh say she is the heir of Khan-Queen Miska herself. The boyars kneel lower than they did. The old women say the girls of her house will be born with the frost in their blood.
I am the heir of Miska.

A rider from the Ice Throne has come with the crown's seal. The hordes of Chaos are in the Tzardom, and the Tzar calls the Great Pulk. Every boyar is to send his rota to the crown at once. The rider waits for an answer.
[From.GetTitledName] refused the Great Pulk while the north burned. Every boyar at court knows it, and every one of them is watching to see what the crown does about it.
Shame his house before the court.
Call him out. Let steel decide it.
Let it pass. There is a war to win.

[Root.GetFirstName] has seized a guest who ate at their table. Bread and salt were given and taken, and in Kislev that is an oath older than the Tzardom. The news is on every road by the end of the week. Boyars who hear it spit on the floor.

Ten years have passed, and it is time for the Ice Queen's Ball. The boyars come in from every oblast in their furs, and at the door each one is given bread and salt by the crown's own hand. Inside there is music and vodka and a thousand candles, and a great deal of watching. Something always happens at the Ice Queen's Ball.
Spare nothing. Let them talk of it for ten years.

Behind a pillar, half drunk, [tsar_ball_rival.GetTitledName] was heard saying the crown would not last the year, and naming the boyars who would help it fall. Half the hall heard it. He has eaten your bread and salt tonight.
Let it pass. He is drunk.

[tsar_ball_kin.GetFirstName] has danced all night with [tsar_ball_match.GetFirstName], the child of [tsar_ball_house.GetTitledName], and they are still talking by the frozen fountain while the musicians pack up. The boyar is already looking at you with hope.

In the middle of a dance [tsar_ball_witch.GetFirstName] stumbled, and when the sleeve fell back there were marks on the arm that no one in the hall wanted to look at. The Ruinous Powers have been dancing at your ball. The Chekist is already at the door.
Burn her. Here, before them all.

When [tsar_ball_witch.GetFirstName] danced past the candles, they froze. The flames stood still in little stalks of ice, and the hall went silent. The gift of ice is in her. The Ice Witches in the hall have seen it too.
